findings.title: Materials' 142% earnings hope is extreme
findings.body: Materials sits at the 37th percentile on forward earnings but the 95th on trailing, a 58-point gap that implies 142 percent growth. That is the market underwriting a near-tripling of profits, a bet that has no precedent in the sector's own five-year history.

findings.title: Health Care's 30-point weekly de-rating
findings.body: Health Care's forward percentile collapsed 29 points in a week and 30 in a month, yet the trailing lens barely moved. The market is rapidly repricing expectations for a sector whose reported earnings still look rich, suggesting the selloff is about forward estimates, not current results.

findings.title: Utilities' percentile collapse outruns multiple
findings.body: Utilities dropped 16 percentile points in a week and 28 in a month on forward valuation, landing at the 28th percentile, while its forward P/E of 17.76 is only 10 percent below trailing. The percentile swing is far larger than the multiple change, meaning the de-rating is mostly relative, not absolute.
